newsitem.title: JAPAN: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 15.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Top Japan business news - Oct 15.

text.p: Three companies including Japan Energy Corp and Itochu Corp will become the first Japanese firms to set up a joint venture in Kuwait to produce a catalyst for desulphurising heavy crude, in cooperation with the Japan International Development Organisation (JAIDO). The new company, capitalised at 2.5 billion yen, will start catalyst production from January 1998 and produce 5,000 tonnes per year. It will formally sign a contract this month.

Citizen Watch Co Ltd is expected to have increased its parent current profit by 32 percent to around 5.5 billion yen in the first half, ended September 30, from a year earlier, helped by a rise in revenues in its watch division and an increase in profit in its information equipment division.
Mitsui & Co Ltd has acquired a controlling interest in Sesa Goa Ltd, a leading Indian iron ore company, by taking over its London-based holding comany.

Eleven leading electronics makers, including Hitachi Ltd, Toshiba Corp and Mitsubishi Electric Corp, plan to test electronic data interchange (EDI) with commercial banks for bill payment from January through March 1997, aiming to cut a large amount of clerical work.

Seiyu Ltd plans to launch a joint venture to operate supermarkets in China in December in cooperation with a Chinese company. It hopes to open the first supermarket by June 1997 in Shanghai, and at least 20 by the year 2000.

Taito Co Ltd hopes to open a computer game centre in Beijing by the end of this year. It has set up a joint venture with two affiliates of Chinese state-owned trust and investment companies in China. The move will put it into competition with Japanese rivals Namco Ltd and Sega Enterprises Ltd. The new company, which is capitalised at two millin dollars, is owned 80 percent by Taito.
